prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for every self-employed person — the right broker depends on your ZIP code, budget, family size, health needs, whether you want ACA/subsidized plans, and whether you want an independent agent who can shop many carriers or a captive agent who sells one carrier’s plans.

How to find a good Kansas City, MO broker who works well for self‑employed people
- Look for an independent agent/broker (not captive to one carrier) so they can compare multiple carriers and plan types.  
- Verify they’re licensed in Missouri (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup).  
- Use reputable directories: Healthcare.gov “Find Local Help,” the National Association of Benefits and Insurance Professionals (NABIP/NAHU) directory, and Google/Yelp reviews.  
- Ask local resources for referrals: CPAs, small-business groups, the KC Chamber, or other self‑employed peers.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Do you specialize in individual/ACA plans and work with self‑employed clients?  
- Are you independent or tied to specific carriers? Which carriers do you represent?  
- How do you get paid (commission vs. client fee)? Any extra cost to me?  
- Can you help me determine subsidy eligibility and estimate premium tax credits?  
- Do you help with plan enrollment, misc forms (1095‑A), and claims issues after enrollment?  
- What is your experience with local provider networks and doctors/hospitals in KC?  
- Can you show a side‑by‑side cost estimate (premiums, deductibles, OOP max) for multiple plans?

Options and alternatives to consider
- ACA Marketplace (healthcare.gov) — often the best for subsidies if your income qualifies. A broker can handle Marketplace enrollment for you.  
- Direct carrier agents — may be OK if you prefer a particular insurer, but you’ll have fewer plan choices.  
- Association plans or professional groups — sometimes cheaper for certain freelancers.  
- Small Group/SHOP — only if you have employees or a spouse you can employ.  
- Short‑term plans — generally not recommended as they don’t meet ACA standards and can leave big gaps.

Next steps I can take for you
- If you share your ZIP code and a few basic details (age, household size, estimated income range, whether you need family coverage or only yourself, any preferred doctors), I can:  
  - look up local independent brokers/agents with good reviews, or  
  - outline specific plans and subsidy estimates for the Marketplace so you know whether a broker’s help is worth it.

If you want, give me your ZIP and a couple of details and I’ll find a few well-rated local brokers and the quickest enrollment options for you.
